title: Casimir connections, braid monodromy and chiral WZW interfaces

items.title: The Casimir tensor is invariant under the diagonal adjoint action
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra, let $B$ be its Killing form, and let $(x_a)$ and $(x^a)$ be $B$-dual bases. The tensor $\Omega:=\sum_a x_a\otimes x^a\in\mathfrak g\otimes\mathfrak g$ corresponds to the identity map under $\Phi_B(u\otimes v)(y):=uB(v,y)$, and is invariant under the diagonal adjoint action:

$$([x,\cdot]\otimes 1+1\otimes[x,\cdot])\Omega=\sum_a [x,x_a]\otimes x^a+x_a\otimes[x,x^a]=0\qquad(x\in\mathfrak g).$$

items.title: The basic form is the Killing form divided by twice the dual Coxeter number
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra with Killing form $B_{\mathrm{Kill}}$. Choose a Cartan subalgebra, a positive root system, its highest root $\theta$, and the Weyl vector $\rho$. Let $B_0:=B_{\mathrm{Kill}}/c$ be the scalar normalization for which the induced form on the root space satisfies $(\theta,\theta)_0=2$; equivalently, define $c:=2/(\theta,\theta)_{\mathrm{Kill}}$, where the root pairing is induced by $B_{\mathrm{Kill}}$. Put $\theta^\vee:=2\theta/(\theta,\theta)_0=\theta$ and $h^\vee:=1+(\rho,\theta^\vee)_0$. Then

$$B_{\mathrm{Kill}}=2h^\vee B_0.$$

items.title: Casimir KZ connection on ordered configurations
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Killing form $B$, let $n\ge2$, and let $V_1,\ldots,V_n$ be finite-dimensional complex vector spaces. A representation here is a complex-linear Lie algebra homomorphism $ho_i:\mathfrak g	o\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_i)$, so $[ho_i(x),ho_i(y)]=ho_i([x,y])$. Let $F_n(\mathbb C)=\{(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\in\mathbb C^n:z_i

e j\}$ be the ordered configuration space and put $V:=V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_n$ in the indicated factor order. For any pair of $B$-dual bases $(x_a),(x^a)$ define $\Omega_{ij}:=\sum_aho_i(x_a)^{(i)}ho_j(x^a)^{(j)}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, where each superscript means that the operator acts on that tensor factor and as the identity on all other factors. For $i<j$ put $\eta_{ij}:=(dz_i-dz_j)/(z_i-z_j)$, a globally defined complex-valued one-form on $F_n(\mathbb C)$. For $\kappa\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, the **Casimir Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection** on the trivial vector bundle $F_n(\mathbb C)	imes V	o F_n(\mathbb C)$ is

$$
abla^{\mathrm{KZ}}_\kappa:=d-\kappa^{-1}\sum_{i<j}\Omega_{ij}\eta_{ij}.$$

Here a connection on this trivial bundle is a complex-linear operator on smooth $V$-valued sections satisfying $
abla(fs)=df\otimes s+f
abla s$ for every smooth scalar function $f$ and section $s$. The associated quadratic Casimir is $C_B:=\sum_a x_ax^a$ in the universal enveloping algebra; with the Killing-form convention above it is central, and $\Omega_{ij}$ is its tensor-level Casimir counterpart.

items.title: Infinitesimal braid identities imply KZ flatness and braid monodromy
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Killing form $B$, let $V_i$ be finite-dimensional complex $\mathfrak g$-modules, and let $\kappa\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$. Fix a basepoint $q\in F_n(\mathbb C)$. On $F_n(\mathbb C)=\{(z_1,\ldots,z_n):z_i
e z_j	ext{ for }i
e j\}$ let $
abla^{\mathrm{KZ}}_\kappa=d-\kappa^{-1}\sum_{i<j}\Omega_{ij}\eta_{ij}$ be the connection defined from the pairwise Casimir tensors $\Omega_{ij}=\sum_aho_i(x_a)^{(i)}ho_j(x^a)^{(j)}$ and forms $\eta_{ij}=(dz_i-dz_j)/(z_i-z_j)$, using $B$-dual bases. Then $
abla^{\mathrm{KZ}}_\kappa$ is flat. Its sheaf of local horizontal sections is a local system with right monodromy action $T$ of the fundamental group of the ordered configuration space based at $q$. With the library convention that $[\alpha][ eta]$ traverses $\alpha$ first and $ eta$ second, the associated left representation is $[\gamma]\mapsto T_{[\gamma]}^{-1}$; on piecewise smooth loops, $T_{[\gamma]}$ is horizontal parallel transport $P_\gamma$. The homeomorphism $z\mapsto z/(1+|z|)$ identifies this fundamental group with the configuration pure braid group. If all $V_i$ are the same module with the same action, simultaneous label and tensor-factor permutation makes the connection equivariant: for $\sigma\in S_n$, set $\sigma\cdot(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=(z_{\sigma^{-1}(1)},\ldots,z_{\sigma^{-1}(n)})$ and $	au_\sigma(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\sigma^{-1}(n)}$, and use $\sigma\cdot(z,v)=(\sigma\cdot z,	au_\sigma v)$. The quotient bundle is $(F_n(\mathbb C)	imes V^{\otimes n})/S_n$ under this action, and the connection descends to the unordered configuration space, giving the corresponding full configuration braid-group representation based at $[q]$. No unitarity or equivalence with a quantum-group ribbon category is asserted.

items.title: Integrable affine modules and conformal-block completion contract
items.statement:
A **chiral Wess–Zumino–Witten (WZW) / vertex-operator-algebra (VOA) completion record** concerns one holomorphic current-algebra sector, not a full left-right theory; it is additional mathematical data and theorems that make a comparison with the finite-dimensional Casimir KZ connection precise. This definition is a contract for such a comparison; it asserts no existence or equivalence theorem.

Fix a compact, connected, simply connected Lie group $G$ with finite-dimensional simple real Lie algebra $\mathfrak g_{\mathbb R}$, and put $\mathfrak g:=\mathfrak g_{\mathbb R}\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$. Choose a Cartan subalgebra and positive roots, let $\theta$ be the highest root, choose the basic invariant form $B_{\mathrm{bas}}$ whose induced root form satisfies $(\theta,\theta)_{\mathrm{bas}}=2$, let $\rho$ be half the sum of the positive roots, and set $h^\vee:=1+(\rho,\theta^\vee)_{\mathrm{bas}}$, where $\theta^\vee:=2\theta/(\theta,\theta)_{\mathrm{bas}}$. The scale lemma on this page gives $B_{\mathrm{Kill}}=2h^\vee B_{\mathrm{bas}}$. Let $\Omega_{\mathrm{bas}}$ and $\Omega_{\mathrm{Kill}}$ denote the pairwise Casimir tensors for these two forms, as in the KZ definition. For a positive integer level $k$, the standard basic-form WZW parameter is $\kappa_{\mathrm{bas}}:=k+h^\vee$. The KZ definition on this page uses the Killing-form tensor, whose tensor is $\Omega_{\mathrm{Kill}}=(2h^\vee)^{-1}\Omega_{\mathrm{bas}}$; therefore its parameter must be $\kappa_{\mathrm{Kill}}:=(k+h^\vee)/(2h^\vee)$ to give the same connection. This is a normalization conversion, not an identification of affine conformal blocks with the finite-dimensional KZ fibers.

Restrict $B_{\mathrm{bas}}$ to the compact real form and use that real invariant symmetric form as $\kappa$ in the smooth-current central extension defined by the cocycle $\omega(X,Y)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}\kappa(X(\theta),Y'(\theta))\,d\theta$. Complexify the extension and restrict its loop algebra to Laurent modes $J_m(x):=xe^{-im\theta}$, $m\in\mathbb Z$. If $K$ is the central generator from the smooth-current extension, set $K_{\mathrm{aff}}:=iK$; then the fixed convention is $[J_m(x),J_n(y)]=J_{m+n}([x,y])+m\delta_{m+n,0}B_{\mathrm{bas}}(x,y)K_{\mathrm{aff}}$. The derivation $d:=i\partial_\theta$ satisfies $[d,J_m(x)]=mJ_m(x)$ and $[d,K_{\mathrm{aff}}]=0$. The resulting central extension with degree derivation is the affine Lie algebra used here. A representation is at level $k$ when $K_{\mathrm{aff}}$ acts as $kI$. After choosing affine Cartan and positive-root data, an **affine highest-weight module** is generated by a vector annihilated by the positive-root subalgebra and on which the Cartan acts by a specified weight whose central coordinate is $k$ and whose degree coordinate is recorded; it is **integrable** when each simple-root Chevalley generator $e_i,f_i$ acts locally nilpotently, meaning that each vector is killed by some positive power of that generator. These are input modules; this definition does not prove their existence or any classification.

For the genus-zero marked curve $\mathbb P^1$ with distinct ordered points $z_1,\ldots,z_n$ and level-$k$ modules $M_1,\ldots,M_n$, put $\mathcal A_{\mathbf z}:=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathcal O(\mathbb P^1\setminus\{z_1,\ldots,z_n\})$, where $\mathcal O$ denotes rational functions with poles only at the marked points. An interface must specify the action of $\mathcal A_{\mathbf z}$ on $M_1\otimes\cdots\otimes M_n$, including the compatible central-extension lift. Given that action, the **coinvariant space** is the quotient of the tensor product by the linear span of all action vectors; its algebraic dual (or a specified continuous dual if a completion is used) is the conformal-block space. A top-level $\mathfrak g$-module is the specified grade-zero subspace relative to the chosen highest-vector degree, with the action of the constant-loop subalgebra; an interface must state that grading convention and prove finite dimensionality before using it as a KZ fiber. Its identification with these varying conformal-block spaces and the analytic continuation maps must be specified rather than inferred from the word “WZW.”

A **sewing datum** specifies, for a curve obtained by joining marked local coordinates, the source and target conformal-block spaces, the intermediate modules, the linear gluing map, and any completion topology and convergence condition. Factorization is a theorem about that datum, not part of this definition. The Sugawara construction means the proposed normally ordered quadratic-current operators that give a Virasoro action; their domains, coefficient convention, and central charge also require a theorem.

For a quantum-group comparison, specify the category with the exact interface of [[def-qftx-braided-line-model]]: it is a locally finite $k$-linear abelian rigid monoidal category over a field $k$, its tensor product is $k$-bilinear, and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)\cong k$; rigid means left and right duals with evaluation and coevaluation maps satisfying the two snake identities. Its braiding $c_{Y,Z}:Y\otimes Z\to Z\otimes Y$ is a natural isomorphism satisfying both hexagon identities with the associator $\alpha_{X,Y,Z}:(X\otimes Y)\otimes Z\to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)$, which satisfies the pentagon identity. For $X$ put $P_0(X)=\mathbf1$, $P_1(X)=X$, and $P_{m+1}(X)=P_m(X)\otimes X$; the positive braid generator acts by the supplier's rebracketed adjacent $c_{X,X}$, with the right input passing over the left. These category and coherence hypotheses are part of the input, not consequences of WZW data.

For a ribbon-fusion comparison, use the exact convention of [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]: $\mathcal C$ is a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit and finitely many simple-object classes, equipped with a braiding and ribbon twist $\theta$. The induced pivotal map is $j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, where $u$ is the Drinfeld morphism supplied by [[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]], and the associated spherical pivotal structure is part of the data. Its trace is $\operatorname{tr}_j(f):=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_X\circ f)$ for $f\in\operatorname{End}(X)$, with the left-trace convention of the same supplier. With simple labels $i,j$, the unnormalized Hopf-link entry is $s_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}_j(c_{j,i}c_{i,j})$, and modularity means this matrix is invertible. No positivity of general quantum dimensions is assumed.

A framing of an oriented link is a homotopy class of nowhere-zero normal vector field along each component; the ribbon twist specifies the operator for one positive unit twist. If a semisimplification is used, state the category and quotient ideal: a morphism $f:X\to Y$ is negligible when $\operatorname{tr}(g\circ f)=0$ for every $g:Y\to X$, using the declared pivotal trace. A claimed equivalence must be a specified monoidal equivalence with coherent structure maps preserving the braiding and twist, together with a proof under its exact hypotheses.

The finite-dimensional KZ flatness theorem concerns finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules and does not by itself establish finite-dimensionality of affine conformal blocks, Sugawara well-definedness, sewing/factorization, or a Drinfeld–Kohno or rational-VOA ribbon-category equivalence. The modularity theorem for the stated $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ root-of-unity quotient establishes modularity of that quotient only; it does not identify its exchanges with WZW monodromy. No generic monodromy unitarity follows.

title: Casimir connections, braid monodromy and chiral WZW interfaces — Examples

items.title: Two-insertion KZ monodromy is a Casimir exponential
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$, let $V=\mathbb C^2$ be its standard representation with its standard Hermitian inner product, and use the Killing-form Casimir tensor $\Omega_{12}$ on $V\otimes V$. For two insertions set $w=z_1-z_2\ne0$. At the basepoint $w_*=1$, take $z_2=0$ and $z_1=w$; along a chosen logarithm branch, a horizontal section with value $v_*$ at $w_*$ is $s(w)=\exp((\Omega_{12}/\kappa)\log(w/w_*))v_*$. The positive loop $w(t)=w_*e^{2\pi i t}$, equivalently $z_1(t)=e^{2\pi i t}$ and $z_2(t)=0$, has horizontal transport

$$P_\gamma=\exp(2\pi i\Omega_{12}/\kappa).$$

For the library's first-then-second fundamental-group product, the associated left monodromy representation uses $P_\gamma^{-1}$; equivalently, $P_\gamma$ is the right monodromy action by horizontal transport. This transport need not be unitary: with $\kappa=i$, it has eigenvalue $e^{\pi/4}$.
